content_types.name: Signal Alert
content_types.desc: A Prophet plan turned into a cashtag post with a price chart showing where we see opportunity.

content_types.name: Chart of the Day
content_types.desc: A single annotated price or macro chart that tells one clear story without commentary.

content_types.name: Plain-English Explainer
content_types.desc: A short thread or post that explains one market concept so a non-professional can act on it.

content_types.name: Macro Note
content_types.desc: A brief plain read on the big picture (rates, liquidity, growth) and what it means right now.

content_types.name: Report Card
content_types.desc: A public update on how a past call played out: the numbers, the outcome, what we learned.

content_types.name: On Our Radar
content_types.desc: A short list of names we're watching closely this week but haven't acted on yet.

content_types.name: Event Reaction
content_types.desc: A fast-turnaround post reacting to a market-moving event with context and what we'd watch next.

content_types.name: Mover of the Day
content_types.desc: The day's single biggest mover, charted, on its cashtag, with the real move %.

content_types.name: Theme Tape
content_types.desc: One post tagged with 6-10 cashtags covering a group that's moving, the reach king at 0 followers.

accounts.name: What changed and why it matters

queue.headline: $WHR never reached the entry
queue.body: 40.8 was the line. The setup never triggered.

$REX closed green for a fourth straight session on 3.8x average volume.
44.3 turned the move away for the fifth time.
That level still caps the move.
Jobless claims are averaging 203k this month, 13.1% below a year ago. The growth scare isn't in the claims data.

queue.headline: $ATR is back at the decision line
queue.body: Above 124 opens the trade. Below 122, the floor is gone.

$AMKR entry 50.3
First objective 63.6
Second objective 76.8
Below 41.5, the structure is gone.

queue.headline: $IPGP is pressing resistance
queue.body: Above 80, the range becomes a breakout.

$STRL sits inside the six-month volume range
Below 442, the rebound loses its structure.
$HAFC held 32, where the recent range did most of its business.

queue.headline: $FIX rejected at 1680 again
queue.body: Its 3rd rejection at the long-term average in the 3-year stretch. The level remains overhead.

queue.headline: $STRL has closed green 3 weeks in a row
queue.body: A hold above 519 makes the move real.

queue.headline: $EBAY finally traded like the level mattered
queue.body: Volume ran 4.2x its recent average as 109, the most-traded price of the past six months, held.

queue.headline: $PPL just lined up a pattern we track.
queue.body: Across every name we test it on, this combination has resolved higher 65% of the time about a month out over its full tested history, over 1990 occurrences universe-wide, not this one name. A measured tendency on a study split, not our trading record. Chart below.

queue.headline: Crypto & Blockchain ripping, +4.0% avg on Friday
queue.body: $BKKT +15.4% $BTDR +15.4% $MARA +13.8% $COIN +11.7% $HOOD +9.1% $RIOT +8.6% $HUT +8.5% $CLSK +8.4% Every name on the list is higher.

accounts.name: Founder's desk: the day's tape, two facts set against each other

queue.body: $ATR has to reclaim 124 before the long case reopens.
The $XRAY long plan failed with its lowest weekly close in 5 years.

$REXR is sitting on the decision line
38.4 has to hold for the move to count.

queue.headline: Growth is firming while inflation stays warm.
queue.body: GDPNow has the economy growing at 5.1% this quarter. Median CPI is running at 2.1%. The tension isn't resolving.

$CLH
323 separates another rejection from a breakout.

accounts.name: Crowd translator — market psychology, mood vs positioning, consumer and tech stories with market consequence

queue.body:
$AMKR needs to hold 50.3 for the recovery to stick.
Below that, it's still base building.

queue.headline: Claims aren't confirming a slowdown.
queue.body: Jobless claims are averaging 203k a week this month, 13.1% below a year ago. Labor remains firm while inflation is still warm.

The crowd is back on $MUSA today
524 has to hold or the attention is early

queue.headline: $EBAY's heaviest volume in months
queue.body: Trading hit 4.2x its recent average while 109, where the most shares changed hands over six months, held. Below 109, the volume surge becomes churn.

queue.headline: $UPWK's hold failed
queue.body: The price where the most shares changed hands in the past six months is back overhead at 8.46. A reclaim repairs the setup.
$SOUN turned away at 7.28 for the 4th time. Still the ceiling.

queue.headline: Semiconductors ripping, +2.9% avg on Friday
queue.body: $SNDK +11.0% $WOLF +7.8% $SIMO +7.4% $LRCX +7.0% $STX +6.9% $AMAT +6.5% $FORM +6.1% $TER +5.2% The whole group is bid, not one name.

queue.body:
Jobless claims: 203k weekly average this month, 13.1% below a year ago
GDPNow: 5.1% annual growth this quarter
Median CPI: 2.1% annual rate
Growth is firming while inflation remains warm.

queue.headline: $HAFC is back within reach of its 5-year high
queue.body: A move through 33.2 would clear the last ceiling.

$ACHC held 27.2.
The same area has found buyers 4 times in 3 years.
Long-term support remains intact.

accounts.name: Mechanism detective — cross-asset disagreement, what moved first, what is already priced, and the missing denominator

queue.body:
$NABL's heaviest volume week in 5 years
demand has to absorb the selling next 🔍
$CMS closed at a fresh yearly low. a reclaim of 68 has to hold to end the selloff.

queue.headline: $WHR stayed below the trigger
queue.body: 40.8 was required before the setup existed. the condition never cleared.
$COHU found buyers at 47.8 again. lose it and the base breaks.

featured_charts.headline: What earns a spot on a list
featured_charts.body: A name earns a slot for a structural reason: a level tested more than once, the tightest range in months, a shelf of volume. Without one of those it is noise.
